Retrieved 2026-07-20 via Exa search highlights.

Brent (Sept delivery) rose ~2-3% to top $90/barrel Monday, highest since 11 June. Reuters/Business Times: Brent +$2.09 (2.37%) to $90.19 by 0241 GMT, touching highest since June 11, after rising 15.9% in the week ended 19 July — biggest weekly gain since April. Guardian: Brent +2.72% to $90.50 by ~0100 GMT after briefly crossing $91. WTI (Aug) ~$83-84, +~2.3%. Asia Business Daily: Brent $90.87 up 3.14%, up ~27% from $71.57 on 1 July.

Cause: US ninth night of strikes + third US service member death + IRGC said two oil tankers exploded/immobilised on "unsafe" southern route through Strait. US enforcing naval blockade on Iranian ports; Iran targeting vessels violating its navigation rules. Four vessels transited Hormuz Sunday, down from eight the previous day (LSEG data).

QUOTE - ING analysts (note, Monday): "ICE Brent broke above US$90 per barrel this morning with no let-up in the escalation in the Gulf."
QUOTE - David Roche, Quantum Strategy (note, Monday, via CNBC): "At this rate of depletion oil inventories get tight in September and even the U.S. gets stressed... Stay long Brent with a target of $95 to $105 a barrel."
